problem: Current main production promotion repeatedly failed at Netlify transport with 401 Unauthorized. A fresh connector authorization could be issued transiently, but the GitHub Actions secret remained stale and the local exact-artifact fallback could not reach the provider from the execution environment.
root_cause: Production authority was split between an expiring GitHub Actions Netlify proxy credential and transient connector-issued authorization. The repository workflow had no safe autonomous credential-rotation path, while the local runner lacked a reliable provider network path.
failed_approaches: Blindly rerunning Production Source Snapshot with the same stale NETLIFY_MCP_PROXY_PATH_TEMP.
Treating the incident as pricing or i18n application failure.
Trying to complete the exact-artifact Netlify CLI fallback from a runtime that could not reliably reach the provider.
Persisting or exposing transient proxy credentials outside a protected secret store.
prevention: Classify Netlify 401 as deploy-auth failure before changing application code.
Retry stale credentials at most once after authoritative classification; then require credential rotation rather than retry loops.
Never put Netlify proxy credentials in repository content, PR bodies, workflow-dispatch inputs, logs, docs or user-visible output.
Preserve the exact current-main production artifact so delivery can resume without rebuilding unrelated code.
If no safe credential-write path and no working direct provider path exist, use BLOCKED_HARD_BOUNDARY rather than claiming live.
After account-level credential recovery, rerun canonical Production Source Snapshot and require exact production SHA plus pricing/i18n browser proof before LIVE_BEWEZEN.
